newsitem.title: USA: Dow vaults higher to end five day skid.
newsitem.headline: Dow vaults higher to end five day skid.

text.p: U.S. blue chips rebounded sharply on Wednesday from their week-long losing streak, propelling the Dow industrials to their sharpest rally in nearly four weeks.
The Dow rose 85 points to close unofficially at 6741 in its best performance since January 3, when it surged 101.60 points.
Even with the solid performance, analysts cautioned, the market appeared to remain on the defensive, with broader and smaller cap indicators failing to match the Dow's gains.
"Today the name of the game was the blue chips," said Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray and Co. "There's still a lot of nervousness in the small cap names."

The cautious mood was also reflected in Nasdaq's performance, said analysts. The technology-laden Nasdaq Composite index managed only a fractional gain to 1355, while drug stocks and other large cap defensive issues fared better.
"Generally, the feeling is that (drug stocks) are a really good place to be," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Van Kampen American Capital.

"The industry has improved its earnings over the last two or three years and the consensus opinion says the economy will slow in the second half of the year," he said. Such a slowdown would not hurt drug companies, which are relatively immune to economic cycles.

Analysts said several upcoming events are pivotal for the market's overall outlook, particularly Friday's fourth quarter U.S. Gross Domestic Product report and tomorrow's scheduled testimony by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan before the Senate Finance Committee.

"Unless one of those events produces a surprise, the market should try to rally here," said Dan Ascani, president and director of research at Global Market Strategists Inc. "A bounce of some kind here would be normal."
But even if stocks do manage a near-term bounce, Ascani said, "We're about out of January now, so the market will probably have a rough road ahead."

The reason is that when January ends, with it may go the huge inflow of retirement fund cash that has provided an important source of market momentum, particularly for large cap stocks which have boomed in recent months.
Analysts did see some reasons to be optimistic that a new rally could be in the making, however, if the economy proves to be more resilient than expected.

"We could have a banner day on Friday with a strong fourth quarter GDP," Froehlich said. "With labor costs not going through the roof and a strong economy, the stock market could decide, 'This looks good for earnings.'"
In individual issues, International Business Machines Corp continued to bounce back from its recent sell-off, gaining 5-1/2 to 156-1/4.
Brinker International Inc slid 4-3/8 to 10-7/8 in the first trading since the company reported disappointing second-quarter earnings. Several Wall Street firms downgraded the shares today.
360 Communications Co fell three to 19 after the company warned of weaker than expected fourth quarter earnings.
Quantum Corp gained 3-1/4 to 36-3/8. Goldman Sachs upgraded the company after it reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings.
The S&P 500 index rose 7.48 to 772.50.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.80 to 1355.17.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
